plan.topic_summary: Flow matching is a class of generative modeling methods that learn vector fields to transport noise to data, offering a potential alternative to diffusion models. For a 1–5 year view, the key question is whether it achieves a meaningful advantage in training stability, inference cost, or sample quality sufficient to displace or complement diffusion-based pipelines in production generative systems.
key_questions: Which major labs and open-source projects have adopted flow matching in production or near-production generative pipelines, and for which modalities (image, video, audio, 3D)?
How does flow matching compare to diffusion models on inference cost (number of function evaluations) and training cost at comparable sample quality, and is the gap widening or narrowing?
What are the known failure modes (mode collapse, training instability, poor extrapolation) and are there architectural or loss-function modifications that reliably mitigate them?
Is flow matching scaling favorably with model size and data volume, or do its theoretical assumptions break down at scale in ways that diffusion does not?
What is the realistic timeline for flow matching to become a default choice in new generative model architectures versus remaining a niche or hybrid component?

sources.title: Flow Matching for Generative Modeling
sources.abstract: We introduce a new paradigm for generative modeling built on Continuous Normalizing Flows (CNFs), allowing us to train CNFs at unprecedented scale. Specifically, we present the notion of Flow Matching (FM), a simulation-free approach for training CNFs based on regressing vector fields of fixed conditional probability paths. Flow Matching is compatible with a general family of Gaussian probability paths for transforming between noise and data samples -- which subsumes existing diffusion paths as specific instances. Interestingly, we find that employing FM with diffusion paths results in a more robust and stable alternative for training diffusion models. Furthermore, Flow Matching opens the door to training CNFs with other, non-diffusion probability paths. An instance of particular interest is using Optimal Transport (OT) displacement interpolation to define the conditional probability paths. These paths are more efficient than diffusion paths, provide faster training and sampling, and result in better generalization. Training CNFs using Flow Matching on ImageNet leads to consistently better performance than alternative diffusion-based methods in terms of both likelihood and sample quality, and allows fast and reliable sample generation using off-the-shelf numerical ODE solvers.

sources.title: Topological Flow Matching
sources.abstract: Flow matching is a powerful generative modeling framework, valued for its simplicity and strong empirical performance. However, its standard formulation treats signals on structured spaces, such as fMRI data on brain graphs, as points in Euclidean space, overlooking the rich topological features of their domains. To address this, we introduce topological flow matching, a topology-aware generalization of flow matching. We interpret flow matching as a framework for solving a degenerate Schrödinger bridge problem and inject topological information by augmenting the reference process with a Laplacian-derived drift. This principled modification captures the structure of the underlying domain while preserving the desirable properties of flow matching: a stable, simulation-free objective and deterministic sample paths. As a result, our framework serves as a drop-in replacement for standard flow matching. We demonstrate its effectiveness on diverse structured datasets, including brain fMRIs, ocean currents, seismic events, and traffic flows.

sources.title: Flow Matching Guide and Code
sources.abstract: Flow Matching (FM) is a recent framework for generative modeling that has achieved state-of-the-art performance across various domains, including image, video, audio, speech, and biological structures. This guide offers a comprehensive and self-contained review of FM, covering its mathematical foundations, design choices, and extensions. By also providing a PyTorch package featuring relevant examples (e.g., image and text generation), this work aims to serve as a resource for both novice and experienced researchers interested in understanding, applying and further developing FM.

sources.title: Alignment Matters Inside and Out in Equivariant Graph Flow Matching
sources.abstract: Graphs are invariant under node permutations, motivating permutation-equivariant architectures in generative models. In flow matching, however, symmetry also affects the source-target coupling: one must choose both which graphs to pair and which node representatives to align. We study these two forms of alignment, termed outer and inner alignment, and their effect on equivariant graph flow matching. We connect inner alignment to transport on the graph quotient space, whose Euclidean quotient metric coincides with Gromov-Monge distance, and show that quotient couplings admit aligned representative lifts while symmetrization yields equivariant flow-matching minimizers, including for categorical endpoints. In practice, we compare random augmentation, permutation-blind minibatch optimal transport, approximate Gromov-Wasserstein alignment, and combinations of inner and outer alignment. Across continuous graph and molecular generation, alignment can substantially simplify trajectories and improve few-step generation, while its benefits depend on the alignment and computational budget. Our results highlight that effective graph flow matching benefits from alignment both inside and across graph pairs.

sources.title: Discrete Flow Matching
sources.abstract: Despite Flow Matching and diffusion models having emerged as powerful generative paradigms for continuous variables such as images and videos, their application to high-dimensional discrete data, such as language, is still limited. In this work, we present Discrete Flow Matching, a novel discrete flow paradigm designed specifically for generating discrete data. Discrete Flow Matching offers several key contributions:(i) it works with a general family of probability paths interpolating between source and target distributions; (ii) it allows for a generic formula for sampling from these probability paths using learned posteriors such as the probability denoiser ($x$-prediction) and noise-prediction ($ε$-prediction); (iii) practically, focusing on specific probability paths defined with different schedulers improves generative perplexity compared to previous discrete diffusion and flow models; and (iv) by scaling Discrete Flow Matching models up to 1.7B parameters, we reach 6.7% Pass@1 and 13.4% Pass@10 on HumanEval and 6.7% Pass@1 and 20.6% Pass@10 on 1-shot MBPP coding benchmarks. Our approach is capable of generating high-quality discrete data in a non-autoregressive fashion, significantly closing the gap between autoregressive models and discrete flow models.

sources.title: Simulation-free Schrödinger bridges via score and flow matching
sources.abstract: We present simulation-free score and flow matching ([SF]$^2$M), a simulation-free objective for inferring stochastic dynamics given unpaired samples drawn from arbitrary source and target distributions. Our method generalizes both the score-matching loss used in the training of diffusion models and the recently proposed flow matching loss used in the training of continuous normalizing flows. [SF]$^2$M interprets continuous-time stochastic generative modeling as a Schrödinger bridge problem. It relies on static entropy-regularized optimal transport, or a minibatch approximation, to efficiently learn the SB without simulating the learned stochastic process. We find that [SF]$^2$M is more efficient and gives more accurate solutions to the SB problem than simulation-based methods from prior work. Finally, we apply [SF]$^2$M to the problem of learning cell dynamics from snapshot data. Notably, [SF]$^2$M is the first method to accurately model cell dynamics in high dimensions and can recover known gene regulatory networks from simulated data. Our code is available in the TorchCFM package at https://github.com/atong01/conditional-flow-matching.

sources.title: Flow Matching in Latent Space
sources.abstract: Flow matching is a recent framework to train generative models that exhibits impressive empirical performance while being relatively easier to train compared with diffusion-based models. Despite its advantageous properties, prior methods still face the challenges of expensive computing and a large number of function evaluations of off-the-shelf solvers in the pixel space. Furthermore, although latent-based generative methods have shown great success in recent years, this particular model type remains underexplored in this area. In this work, we propose to apply flow matching in the latent spaces of pretrained autoencoders, which offers improved computational efficiency and scalability for high-resolution image synthesis. This enables flow-matching training on constrained computational resources while maintaining their quality and flexibility. Additionally, our work stands as a pioneering contribution in the integration of various conditions into flow matching for conditional generation tasks, including label-conditioned image generation, image inpainting, and semantic-to-image generation. Through extensive experiments, our approach demonstrates its effectiveness in both quantitative and qualitative results on various datasets, such as CelebA-HQ, FFHQ, LSUN Church & Bedroom, and ImageNet. We also provide a theoretical control of the Wasserstein-2 distance between the reconstructed latent flow distribution and true data distribution, showing it is upper-bounded by the latent flow matching objective. Our code will be available at https://github.com/VinAIResearch/LFM.git.

sources.title: Flow Matching for Scalable Simulation-Based Inference
sources.abstract: Neural posterior estimation methods based on discrete normalizing flows have become established tools for simulation-based inference (SBI), but scaling them to high-dimensional problems can be challenging. Building on recent advances in generative modeling, we here present flow matching posterior estimation (FMPE), a technique for SBI using continuous normalizing flows. Like diffusion models, and in contrast to discrete flows, flow matching allows for unconstrained architectures, providing enhanced flexibility for complex data modalities. Flow matching, therefore, enables exact density evaluation, fast training, and seamless scalability to large architectures--making it ideal for SBI. We show that FMPE achieves competitive performance on an established SBI benchmark, and then demonstrate its improved scalability on a challenging scientific problem: for gravitational-wave inference, FMPE outperforms methods based on comparable discrete flows, reducing training time by 30% with substantially improved accuracy. Our work underscores the potential of FMPE to enhance performance in challenging inference scenarios, thereby paving the way for more advanced applications to scientific problems.

sources.title: Equivariant flow matching
sources.abstract: Normalizing flows are a class of deep generative models that are especially interesting for modeling probability distributions in physics, where the exact likelihood of flows allows reweighting to known target energy functions and computing unbiased observables. For instance, Boltzmann generators tackle the long-standing sampling problem in statistical physics by training flows to produce equilibrium samples of many-body systems such as small molecules and proteins. To build effective models for such systems, it is crucial to incorporate the symmetries of the target energy into the model, which can be achieved by equivariant continuous normalizing flows (CNFs). However, CNFs can be computationally expensive to train and generate samples from, which has hampered their scalability and practical application. In this paper, we introduce equivariant flow matching, a new training objective for equivariant CNFs that is based on the recently proposed optimal transport flow matching. Equivariant flow matching exploits the physical symmetries of the target energy for efficient, simulation-free training of equivariant CNFs. We demonstrate the effectiveness of flow matching on rotation and permutation invariant many-particle systems and a small molecule, alanine dipeptide, where for the first time we obtain a Boltzmann generator with significant sampling efficiency without relying on tailored internal coordinate featurization. Our results show that the equivariant flow matching objective yields flows with shorter integration paths, improved sampling efficiency, and higher scalability compared to existing methods.

sources.title: Flow Matching Ergodic Coverage
sources.abstract: Ergodic coverage effectively generates exploratory behaviors for embodied agents by aligning the spatial distribution of the agent's trajectory with a target distribution, where the difference between these two distributions is measured by the ergodic metric. However, existing ergodic coverage methods are constrained by the limited set of ergodic metrics available for control synthesis, fundamentally limiting their performance. In this work, we propose an alternative approach to ergodic coverage based on flow matching, a technique widely used in generative inference for efficient and scalable sampling. We formally derive the flow matching problem for ergodic coverage and show that it is equivalent to a linear quadratic regulator problem with a closed-form solution. Our formulation enables alternative ergodic metrics from generative inference that overcome the limitations of existing ones. These metrics were previously infeasible for control synthesis but can now be supported with no computational overhead. Specifically, flow matching with the Stein variational gradient flow enables control synthesis directly over the score function of the target distribution, improving robustness to the unnormalized distributions; on the other hand, flow matching with the Sinkhorn divergence flow enables an optimal transport-based ergodic metric, improving coverage performance on non-smooth distributions with irregular supports. We validate the improved performance and competitive computational efficiency of our method through comprehensive numerical benchmarks and across different nonlinear dynamics. We further demonstrate the practicality of our method through a series of drawing and erasing tasks on a Franka robot.

sources.title: On the Guidance of Flow Matching
sources.abstract: Flow matching has shown state-of-the-art performance in various generative tasks, ranging from image generation to decision-making, where generation under energy guidance (abbreviated as guidance in the following) is pivotal. However, the guidance of flow matching is more general than and thus substantially different from that of its predecessor, diffusion models. Therefore, the challenge in guidance for general flow matching remains largely underexplored. In this paper, we propose the first framework of general guidance for flow matching. From this framework, we derive a family of guidance techniques that can be applied to general flow matching. These include a new training-free asymptotically exact guidance, novel training losses for training-based guidance, and two classes of approximate guidance that cover classical gradient guidance methods as special cases. We theoretically investigate these different methods to give a practical guideline for choosing suitable methods in different scenarios. Experiments on synthetic datasets, image inverse problems, and offline reinforcement learning demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed guidance methods and verify the correctness of our flow matching guidance framework. Code to reproduce the experiments can be found at https://github.com/AI4Science-WestlakeU/flow_guidance.

sources.title: Generalized Wasserstein Flow Matching: Nested Couplings for Point Cloud Generation
sources.abstract: We formulate flow matching on probability measures over probability measures. Directly from the Wasserstein-on-Wasserstein (WoW) continuity equation, we show that admissible nested outer and inner couplings induce a valid metameasure flow and non-local velocity field. Validity requires neither optimal plans nor a smooth manifold. Practically, this opens up the design space of multisample flow matching: exact Wasserstein plans are distinguished by energy and straightness, while sliced and lazy linear plans yield scalable alternatives. Point-cloud experiments, including controlled Bures-Wasserstein and Euclidean minibatch baselines, demonstrate the resulting geometry-cost trade-off.

sources.title: $λ$-Controlled GRPO: Turning Flow-Matching Ratio Instability into a Budgeted Resource
sources.abstract: Reinforcement learning is increasingly used to align image generators with reward signals, and Flow-GRPO recently extended this paradigm to flow-matching models by treating the denoising sampler as a stochastic policy that can be optimized from reward feedback. Training in this setting is unstable in a way specific to multi-step denoising: the policy update changes systematically across denoising steps, with importance ratios drifting below one, becoming increasingly dispersed, clipping at different rates, and leaving fewer usable samples late in training. Prior work treats these effects as separate failure modes and addresses each with a hand-tuned stabilizer. We show instead that they arise from a single per-step quantity, which we call path variance. This quantity is determined exactly by the sampler's Gaussian transition kernel and can be estimated cheaply during training. This reframes instability as a resource that can be measured and budgeted rather than a collection of symptoms to repair. Our method, $λ$-Controlled GRPO, calibrates importance-ratio behavior from this predicted law rather than from noisy empirical statistics, and allocates gradient effort across denoising steps according to their predicted cost. The two scales governing the update are fixed by standard policy choices rather than introduced as free tuning parameters. On a text-to-image model under two reward settings, rendering difficult target text scored by optical character recognition and matching human preferences scored by a preference model, $λ$-Controlled GRPO improves both text accuracy and preference reward over the strongest empirical stabilizer. It also keeps late-step path variance within its intended budget, precisely where the baseline systematically overshoots. The result is a Flow-GRPO update calibrated by its own transition law rather than stabilized after instability appears.

sources.title: Prediction--Loss Alignment for Sampler--Robust Flow Matching Training
sources.abstract: Recent work has popularized a practical recipe in diffusion and flow matching: predict the clean signal $x$, convert it to a velocity, and train through a velocity-space loss. The conversion contains a singular endpoint amplification and therefore appears prone to unstable optimization, yet recent systems obtain strong empirical results with this recipe. We investigate this tension through the integrability of the pre-optimizer stochastic-gradient second moment. Under stated initialization conditions, the moment diverges under Uniform sampling; boundary-suppressing sampling can restore integrability under an additional upper-growth condition. We then show that prediction--loss alignment eliminates this conversion-induced source of non-integrability. Under a uniform moment bound, alignment yields a finite second moment for every timestep density, including Uniform sampling. Controlled experiments across continuous and binary settings reproduce the predicted sampler-dependent instability and show that aligned objectives remain trainable across the tested samplers. These results reconcile pointwise amplification with sampler-dependent empirical success and support alignment as a principled route to more robust flow-matching training.

sources.title: Learning Straight Flows: Variational Flow Matching for Efficient Generation
sources.abstract: Flow Matching has limited ability in achieving one-step generation due to its reliance on learned curved trajectories. Previous studies have attempted to address this limitation by either modifying the coupling distribution to prevent interpolant intersections or introducing consistency and mean-velocity modeling to promote straight trajectory learning. However, these approaches often suffer from discrete approximation errors, training instability, and convergence difficulties. To tackle these issues, in the present work, we propose \textbf{S}traight \textbf{V}ariational \textbf{F}low \textbf{M}atching (\textbf{S-VFM}), which integrates a variational latent code representing the ``generation overview'' into the Flow Matching framework. \textbf{S-VFM} explicitly enforces trajectory straightness, ideally producing linear generation paths. The proposed method achieves competitive performance across three challenge benchmarks and demonstrates advantages in both training and inference efficiency compared with existing methods.

sources.title: Training Flow Matching: The Role of Weighting and Parameterization
sources.abstract: We study the training objectives of denoising-based generative models, with a particular focus on loss weighting and output parameterization, including noise-, clean image-, and velocity-based formulations. Through a systematic numerical study, we analyze how these training choices interact with the intrinsic dimensionality of the data manifold, model architecture, and dataset size. Our experiments span synthetic datasets with controlled geometry as well as image data, and compare training objectives using quantitative metrics for denoising accuracy (PSNR across noise levels) and generative quality (FID). Rather than proposing a new method, our goal is to disentangle the various factors that matter when training a flow matching model, in order to provide practical insights on design choices.

sources.title: Reinforce Adjoint Matching: Scaling RL Post-Training of Diffusion and Flow-Matching Models
sources.abstract: Diffusion and flow-matching models scale because pretraining is supervised regression: a clean sample is noised analytically, and a model regresses against a closed-form target. RL post-training aligns the model with a reward. In image generation, this makes samples compose objects correctly, render text legibly, and match human preferences. Existing methods rely on costly SDE rollouts, reward gradients, or surrogate losses, sacrificing pretraining's regression structure. We show that the structure extends to RL post-training. Under KL-regularized reward maximization, the optimal generative process tilts the clean-endpoint distribution towards samples with higher reward and leaves the noising law unchanged. Combining this with the adjoint-matching optimality condition and a REINFORCE identity, we derive Reinforce Adjoint Matching (RAM): a consistency loss that corrects the pretraining target with the reward. At each step, we draw a clean endpoint from the current model, evaluate its reward, noise it as in pretraining, and regress. No SDE rollouts, backward adjoint sweeps, or reward gradients are required. Like the pretraining objective, RAM is simple and scales. On Stable Diffusion 3.5M, RAM achieves the highest reward on composability, text rendering, and human preference, reaching Flow-GRPO's peak reward in up to $50\times$ fewer training steps.

sources.title: Consistency Flow Matching: Defining Straight Flows with Velocity Consistency
sources.abstract: Flow matching (FM) is a general framework for defining probability paths via Ordinary Differential Equations (ODEs) to transform between noise and data samples. Recent approaches attempt to straighten these flow trajectories to generate high-quality samples with fewer function evaluations, typically through iterative rectification methods or optimal transport solutions. In this paper, we introduce Consistency Flow Matching (Consistency-FM), a novel FM method that explicitly enforces self-consistency in the velocity field. Consistency-FM directly defines straight flows starting from different times to the same endpoint, imposing constraints on their velocity values. Additionally, we propose a multi-segment training approach for Consistency-FM to enhance expressiveness, achieving a better trade-off between sampling quality and speed. Preliminary experiments demonstrate that our Consistency-FM significantly improves training efficiency by converging 4.4x faster than consistency models and 1.7x faster than rectified flow models while achieving better generation quality. Our code is available at: https://github.com/YangLing0818/consistency_flow_matching

sources.title: FACM: Flow-Anchored Consistency Models
sources.abstract: Continuous-time Consistency Models (CMs) promise efficient few-step generation but face significant challenges with training instability. We argue this instability stems from a fundamental conflict: Training the network exclusively on a shortcut objective leads to the catastrophic forgetting of the instantaneous velocity field that defines the flow. Our solution is to explicitly anchor the model in the underlying flow, ensuring high trajectory fidelity during training. We introduce the Flow-Anchored Consistency Model (FACM), where a Flow Matching (FM) task serves as a dynamic anchor for the primary CM shortcut objective. Key to this Flow-Anchoring approach is a novel expanded time interval strategy that unifies optimization for a single model while decoupling the two tasks to ensure stable, architecturally-agnostic training. By distilling a pre-trained LightningDiT model, our method achieves a state-of-the-art FID of 1.32 with two steps (NFE=2) and 1.70 with just one step (NFE=1) on ImageNet 256x256. To address the challenge of scalability, we develop a memory-efficient Chain-JVP that resolves key incompatibilities with FSDP. This method allows us to scale FACM training on a 14B parameter model (Wan 2.2), accelerating its Text-to-Image inference from 2x40 to 2-8 steps. Our code and pretrained models: https://github.com/ali-vilab/FACM.

sources.title: Inductive Moment Matching
sources.abstract: Diffusion models and Flow Matching generate high-quality samples but are slow at inference, and distilling them into few-step models often leads to instability and extensive tuning. To resolve these trade-offs, we propose Inductive Moment Matching (IMM), a new class of generative models for one- or few-step sampling with a single-stage training procedure. Unlike distillation, IMM does not require pre-training initialization and optimization of two networks; and unlike Consistency Models, IMM guarantees distribution-level convergence and remains stable under various hyperparameters and standard model architectures. IMM surpasses diffusion models on ImageNet-256x256 with 1.99 FID using only 8 inference steps and achieves state-of-the-art 2-step FID of 1.98 on CIFAR-10 for a model trained from scratch.

sources.title: Mean Flow Distillation: Robust and Stable Distillation for Flow Matching Models
sources.abstract: Flow Matching models have demonstrated strong performance across a wide range of generative tasks. However, their reliance on ODE-based iterative sampling incurs substantial computational overhead in inference, which limits their applicability in real-time scenes. While distillation is a promising solution, existing approaches largely borrow from diffusion-based score matching, often failing to exploit the intrinsic geometric structure of flows and suffering from training instability, high variance, and degraded generation quality. In this paper, we propose Mean Flow Distillation (MFD), a novel distillation framework tailored for flow matching models. We theoretically demonstrate that MFD acts as a temporal low-pass filter, effectively suppressing the high-frequency optimization noise inherent in variational score distillation (VSD) while ensuring global trajectory consistency. We further prove the Mean Flow Matching Theorem, establishing that matching expected average velocities is sufficient for strict distribution alignment. Empirically, on challenging tasks of high-dimensional manifolds including 4D occupancy forecasting and text-to-image generation, MFD achieves state-of-the-art performance, enabling high-fidelity single-step generation.

sources.title: An Introduction to Flow Matching and Diffusion Models
sources.abstract: Diffusion and flow-based models have become the state of the art for generative AI across a wide range of data modalities, including images, videos, shapes, molecules, music, and more. This tutorial provides a self-contained introduction to diffusion and flow-based generative models from first principles. We systematically develop the necessary mathematical background in ordinary and stochastic differential equations and derive the core algorithms of flow matching and denoising diffusion models. We then provide a step-by-step guide to building image and video generators, including training methods, guidance, and architectural design. This course is ideal for machine learning researchers who want to develop a principled understanding of the theory and practice of generative AI.

sources.title: Flow Matching for Plasma Vertical Position Control
sources.venue: International Conference on Advanced Algorithms and Control Engineering (ICAACE)
sources.abstract: Plasma elongation improves confinement but increases susceptibility to vertical instability, requiring rapid stabilization. Classical model-based controllers often lack precision and robustness, motivating data-driven approaches that learn system dynamics from operational data. We propose a Flow Matching generative model to produce future control sequences conditioned on the current plasma state and reference trajectory. Compared with diffusion models, Flow Matching generates high-quality trajectories with fewer numerical integration steps, reducing inference latency. Training data and simulations are generated using the RZIp plasma response model. Results show that the Flow-Matching-based controller achieves robust and fast vertical position regulation. This framework offers a practical and efficient approach for future real-time plasma control.

sources.title: Flow Generator Matching
sources.abstract: In the realm of Artificial Intelligence Generated Content (AIGC), flow-matching models have emerged as a powerhouse, achieving success due to their robust theoretical underpinnings and solid ability for large-scale generative modeling. These models have demonstrated state-of-the-art performance, but their brilliance comes at a cost. The process of sampling from these models is notoriously demanding on computational resources, as it necessitates the use of multi-step numerical ordinary differential equations (ODEs). Against this backdrop, this paper presents a novel solution with theoretical guarantees in the form of Flow Generator Matching (FGM), an innovative approach designed to accelerate the sampling of flow-matching models into a one-step generation, while maintaining the original performance. On the CIFAR10 unconditional generation benchmark, our one-step FGM model achieves a new record Fréchet Inception Distance (FID) score of 3.08 among few-step flow-matching-based models, outperforming original 50-step flow-matching models. Furthermore, we use the FGM to distill the Stable Diffusion 3, a leading text-to-image flow-matching model based on the MM-DiT architecture. The resulting MM-DiT-FGM one-step text-to-image model demonstrates outstanding industry-level performance. When evaluated on the GenEval benchmark, MM-DiT-FGM has delivered remarkable generating qualities, rivaling other multi-step models in light of the efficiency of a single generation step.

findings.claim: Training instability recurs across the flow-matching literature: RL post-training, few-step distillation, consistency-style training and the clean-signal-to-velocity loss are each reported as unstable. This suggests the stability problems are structural, not isolated.
findings.label: ai_interpretation
findings.rationale: Five separate abstracts describe instability, divergence, or training difficulty in different parts of the pipeline. All are abstract-only, and most are arXiv preprints that are not peer reviewed (FACM and Mean Flow Distillation are conference papers). Each paper also proposes its own fix, so the instability framing may partly motivate the novelty claim. The evidence is therefore indirect for the claim that these problems are unresolved in practice.

findings.claim: The RL alignment stage for flow-matching image generators is described as unstable across denoising steps: importance ratios drift below one, become dispersed, clip at different rates, and leave fewer usable samples late in training. Earlier fixes were hand-tuned stabilizers.
findings.label: verified_fact
findings.rationale: This restates the abstract's account of failure modes in Flow-GRPO-style training. It is a single arXiv preprint with zero citations, so the diagnosis and the proposed fix are not independently validated.
findings.supporting_excerpt: importance ratios drifting below one, becoming increasingly dispersed, clipping at different rates, and leaving fewer usable samples late in training

findings.claim: A common training recipe (predict the clean signal, convert it to a velocity, train with a velocity-space loss) has a singular endpoint amplification. Under stated conditions the stochastic-gradient second moment diverges under Uniform timestep sampling, so outcomes depend on the sampler.
findings.label: verified_fact
findings.rationale: The result is theoretical, with controlled experiments in continuous and binary settings. The abstract does not report large-scale image or video models, so applicability to production systems is a gap. It is an arXiv preprint.
findings.supporting_excerpt: Under stated initialization conditions, the moment diverges under Uniform sampling; boundary-suppressing sampling can restore integrability under an additional upper-growth condition.

findings.claim: Straight-path and few-step flow methods carry costs. Flow matching is said to be limited for one-step generation because of its curved trajectories. Prior straightening and consistency approaches are said to suffer discrete approximation errors, instability and convergence difficulties.
findings.label: verified_fact
findings.rationale: This is the authors' characterization of prior work in a motivating paragraph, from an arXiv preprint, not a controlled comparison. Reports of 'competitive performance' on three benchmarks leave open how the method compares at scale.
findings.supporting_excerpt: Flow Matching has limited ability in achieving one-step generation due to its reliance on learned curved trajectories.

findings.claim: Headline few-step results rest on narrow benchmarks (ImageNet 256, CIFAR-10) and often on distillation from a pretrained teacher. The inference-cost advantage may therefore depend on an expensive multi-step teacher, and the metrics may not generalize to other modalities.
findings.label: ai_interpretation
findings.rationale: FACM distills a pre-trained LightningDiT, FGM distills Stable Diffusion 3, and IMM and FGM report FID on CIFAR-10 and ImageNet. FID is a single proxy metric, and the abstracts give no compute or total-cost accounting. FGM is an arXiv preprint. IMM trains from scratch, which partly counters the teacher dependence.

findings.claim: The reported scalable-training result needed bespoke engineering: a memory-efficient Chain-JVP was built to resolve incompatibilities with FSDP when scaling consistency training to a 14B-parameter model. This implies that scaling these methods is non-trivial.
findings.label: ai_interpretation
findings.rationale: The inference rests on one abstract that mentions a key incompatibility with FSDP. Any dependence on specific frameworks or on other hardware cost is not reported.

findings.claim: Reported gains are often evidenced by preliminary or small-scale experiments and relative speedups, and are not yet independently reproduced. Examples are the '4.4x' and '1.7x' convergence speedups and the '50x fewer steps' to match Flow-GRPO's peak reward.
findings.label: ai_interpretation
findings.rationale: The Consistency-FM abstract itself calls its experiments 'preliminary'. The RAM claim compares against one baseline on Stable Diffusion 3.5M and gives no wall-clock or reward-hacking analysis in the abstract. Both are arXiv preprints, and their comparisons are not independently replicated.

findings.claim: Evidence for flow matching in safety-critical control is thin. The plasma vertical-control study relies on data and simulations generated from the RZIp response model, and no hardware validation is mentioned.
findings.label: verified_fact
findings.rationale: This is a single simulation-only conference abstract, with no reported comparison against classical controllers on quantitative metrics. The 'robust' claim is not validated beyond the simulator, which is a gap rather than evidence of failure.
findings.supporting_excerpt: Training data and simulations are generated using the RZIp plasma response model.

findings.claim: Training design choices such as loss weighting and output parameterization interact with data-manifold dimensionality, architecture and dataset size. This implies recipes may not transfer across settings and require tuning.
findings.label: ai_interpretation
findings.rationale: The abstract describes a numerical study of these interactions but gives no specific results. The inference about non-transferability is mine. It is an arXiv preprint.

hype_flags: 'State-of-the-art' FID claims on ImageNet-256 and CIFAR-10 rest on one proxy metric and benchmark.
'Robust' and 'stable' training claims appear in many abstracts with no independent replication and mostly lack failure-case analysis.
'Industry-level performance' for one-step text-to-image distillation, based on GenEval in an abstract only.
'Up to 50x fewer training steps' is a step-count comparison, not compute or wall-clock.
'Practical and efficient approach for real-time plasma control' is supported only by simulation.

finding.claim: S2 overstates the discrete flow matching result. The cited abstract says the approach narrows the gap to autoregressive models, not that it is competitive with them. The 6.7% Pass@1 on HumanEval is a low absolute score, and the abstract offers no head-to-head comparison with an autoregressive baseline of similar size.
finding.label: ai_interpretation
finding.rationale: Closing the gap implies the models are still behind. The 'competitive at scale' wording is not supported by the abstract, and a 6.7% Pass@1 does not show parity. Only the abstract was reviewed.
finding.supporting_excerpt: significantly closing the gap between autoregressive models and discrete flow models.

finding.claim: S1 and S11 present flow matching as uniformly robust and state-of-the-art, but they omit the documented training-instability caveats. The claim that FM is a 'more robust and stable' training route comes from the original authors. Later work reports sampler-dependent gradient divergence for a common x-prediction-to-velocity recipe, and also reports instability in RL post-training and few-step distillation. The 'state-of-the-art across domains' claim in S11 is the guide's own self-description, not independent evidence.

finding.rationale: The divergence applies to a specific training recipe, not to FM in general. It still shows that the stability claim needs conditions attached. Taken together with the RL-stage and distillation instability reports, it suggests a recurring pattern. The guide abstract (src_48ea58bf3a) asserts SOTA without presenting any evidence.

finding.claim: S4 inflates the latent-space claim. The abstract reports 'improved' efficiency, not 'substantial' improvement, and gives no quantified comparison in the visible text. finding.claim: S3 is labelled a verified_fact and rated medium confidence, but it rests on a single abstract-only 2026 preprint. finding.label: ai_interpretation

limitations: Only 12 abstract-only records were provided, with no full-text verification of methods, ablations, or compute costs.
Many papers are arXiv preprints and are not peer reviewed; several have near-zero citations, so influence is unproven.
Search was risk-oriented but returned mostly method papers with self-reported limitations, with little independent evidence on failures, reproducibility, or deployment.

The evidence set is small (24 papers) and was retrieved around risk themes. The absence of contradicting papers for S5, S7, S9 and S10 reflects that limited coverage, not confirmation, so I left those findings unchallenged.

The method includes generating separated time-domain audio signals based on the refined separated source embeddings from the hybrid mask module.

sources.abstract: The invention relates to the technical field of artificial intelligence, in particular to a marine drug reaction generation method and system based on mechanism perception and flow matching, and the method comprises the following steps: respectively carrying out characterization coding on a drug three-dimensional conformation and a cell line expression profile to obtain drug characterization and cell line characterization; constructing a target protein relation graph based on the target protein set, and performing graph message passing on the initial representation in the target protein relation graph to obtain a target protein graph representation; inputting the drug characterization and the target protein map characterization into a multi-head attention mechanism predictor to obtain a constructed drug target binding spectrum; and performing multi-head cross attention on the drug target combination spectrum and the cell line characterization to obtain an interactive semantic signal, performing activation function and gating function on the interactive semantic signal and the drug characterization to obtain a condition vector, splicing the condition vector and a noise sample, and inputting the spliced condition vector and the noise sample into the trained velocity field prediction network to obtain a complete response spectrum. The method is suitable for predicting and screening the anticancer activity of candidate drugs which are novel in structure and scarce in data.

sources.title: Target state flow matched single cell development dynamic prediction system and prediction method thereof [CN122867769A]
sources.abstract: The invention discloses a single cell development dynamic prediction system based on target state flow matching and a prediction method thereof, and belongs to the technical field of biological single cell modeling. The system comprises a data loading and protocol analysis module, a fixed hypervariant gene space construction module, a time condition Transform coding module, an online optimal transmission pairing module, a target state flow matching training module and a prediction generation module. According to the method, a target state re-parameterization flow matching structure is adopted, a target end point is explicitly predicted, and a velocity field is deduced; a generalization transfer relation is learned through source and target biological time dual condition coding; carrying out pairing processing on the unpaired single cell snapshots by adopting online Sinkhorn; the flow matching loss, the multi-space distribution distance and the mean value matching constraint are jointly used. According to the method, cell expression distribution at unobserved time points can be generated under the condition of no real cell pairing, and meanwhile, the consistency of the cell level and the population level is ensured.

sources.title: Segmentation hydraulic system of sugarcane harvester [CN122857513A]
authors: GUANGXI LIUGONG AGRICULTURAL MACHINERY CO LTD
sources.organization: GUANGXI LIUGONG AGRICULTURAL MACHINERY CO LTD
sources.abstract: The invention discloses a hydraulic sectioning system of a sugarcane harvester, and belongs to the technical field of hydraulic systems of agricultural machinery. A traditional low-speed large-torque cycloid sectioning motor structure is abandoned, a high-speed small-displacement gear motor is matched with a large-speed-ratio planetary reducer to form a planet row structure, and an original sectioning motor is replaced; and meanwhile, a traditional gear double-pump oil supply structure is optimized into a single-pump oil supply structure, a system shunt motor is omitted, and accurate flow matching of the sectioning motor and the channel motor is achieved. Hydraulic oil backflow pressure relief is not needed, ineffective power loss is thoroughly eliminated, hydraulic pipeline layout is greatly simplified, the equipment manufacturing cost is reduced, the working condition of uniform cutting of sugarcanes is completely met, the working requirements of domestic, Southeast Asia, South America and other overseas sugarcane main producing areas are met, and the working efficiency is improved. And meanwhile, the device can be popularized to various mechanical equipment with flow matching difficulty of upper and lower hydraulic motors, such as a drilling machine, and is extremely high in universality and practicability.

sources.title: Visual model rapid self-adaption method and system based on multi-modal generation prior [CN122866758A]
sources.abstract: The invention discloses a visual model rapid self-adaption method and system based on multi-modal generation prior, and belongs to the technical field of computer visual model self-adaption. Cooperative work is carried out based on a pre-training discrimination model and a class condition flow matching generation model. Dynamically sampling and selecting a current effective time step from the candidate generation time steps; constructing a disturbance sample and a target speed, obtaining a speed prediction value under each category condition, constructing a speed consistency loss with the target speed after category probability weighted aggregation, and updating a discrimination model parameter; and calculating an unsupervised reward based on the sorting consistency of the discriminated score and the generated score, and updating a time step selection strategy. Target domain labeling is not needed, different distribution offsets can be dynamically adapted, and the robustness and the self-adaption efficiency of a visual model in a real deployment environment are effectively improved.

sources.title: Nano antibody conjugate de novo design method and device based on reasoning stage sequential reward guidance [CN122867773A]
sources.abstract: The invention relates to the technical field of biological information, in particular to a nano antibody conjugate de novo design method and device based on reasoning stage sequential reward guidance. The method comprises the following steps: acquiring slot length information of a target antigen three-dimensional structure, an epitope hot spot, a humanized nano antibody frame region and a complementary determining region, and generating the complementary determining region and a docking pose by utilizing a partial hidden variable flow matching generation model with an alpha carbon coordinate channel and a hidden variable channel of each residue; performing predictive final-state trial calculation on a plurality of middle check points of the sampling track, constructing a composite reward according to at least two of an interface prediction index, a pose consistency index and an epitope contact coverage index, and performing sequential resampling according to a temperature modulation probability; in the sampling process, a humanized framework structure is maintained, and multi-index screening and structure redundancy removal are carried out at an end point. According to the method, the generation proportion of the high-quality candidates is improved in the reasoning stage without re-training to generate the backbone.

sources.title: Cross-domain few-sample fault diagnosis method and device based on optimal transmission and stream matching [CN122839096A]
sources.abstract: The invention discloses a cross-domain few-sample fault diagnosis method and device based on optimal transmission and flow matching, and relates to the technical field of bearing fault diagnosis, and the method comprises the steps: constructing a prototype network; training the prototype network; inputting a to-be-diagnosed sample into the trained prototype network to generate a fault diagnosis result; the training step comprises the following steps: mapping a support set into a support feature set; calculating a mean value prototype and a covariance prototype; constructing a cost matrix between the source domain and the target domain; an optimal transmission algorithm is adopted, and the optimal transmission matrix of each category is solved according to the cost matrix; modeling a migration process from a source domain to a target domain in each category by adopting a flow matching mechanism so as to correct a source domain support feature set; correcting a mean value prototype and a covariance prototype; and optimizing the prototype network according to the corrected source domain support feature set, the mean value prototype and the covariance prototype. By adopting the method, the stability and robustness of few-sample fault identification under the strong domain offset condition can be improved.

sources.title: Multi-stage 3D generation model alignment method and system based on preference feedback loop, and readable storage medium [CN122841609A]
authors: SCHOOL OF SOFTWARE TECHNOLOGY NINGBO INNOVATION AND MANAGEMENT CENTER OF ZHEJIANG UNIV
sources.organization: SCHOOL OF SOFTWARE TECHNOLOGY NINGBO INNOVATION AND MANAGEMENT CENTER OF ZHEJIANG UNIV
sources.abstract: The invention discloses a multi-stage 3D generation model alignment method and system based on a preference feedback loop and a readable storage medium. The method comprises the following steps: firstly, performing direct preference optimization based on flow matching on a subsequent structured latent variable generation model based on a preference data set to obtain an optimized structured latent variable generation model; respectively generating optimized 3D assets and non-optimized 3D assets under the same text cue word by utilizing the optimized structured latent variable generation model and the parameter-frozen structured latent variable generation model, and constructing a cross-stage preference sample pair; and then obtaining a high-quality cross-stage preference sample through quality weight screening and preference weight weighting, and converting the high-quality cross-stage preference sample into sparse structure representation for training a preorder sparse structure generation model. Therefore, the subsequent preference optimization signal is transmitted to the preorder structure generation stage, a preference feedback loop is formed, the problem of gradient propagation interruption caused by non-micromanipulation in the multi-stage 3D generation process is relieved, and the human preference alignment effect of generated 3D assets in the aspects of geometric structures, texture details and text consistency is improved.

sources.title: Unmanned aerial vehicle overlooking pedestrian trajectory prediction method based on flow matching [CN122821425A]
authors: ZHONGKE HUACHUANG HANGZHOU TECH CO LTD
sources.organization: ZHONGKE HUACHUANG HANGZHOU TECH CO LTD
sources.abstract: The invention belongs to the field of image or video recognition, and particularly discloses an unmanned aerial vehicle overlooking pedestrian trajectory prediction method based on stream matching, which comprises the following steps: S1, obtaining pedestrian pixel historical trajectories corresponding to an unmanned aerial vehicle overlooking video stream, an unmanned aerial vehicle flight height and a camera focal length, based on a camera imaging geometrical relationship, pixel displacement is converted into a rice system motion feature with a unified physical scale, and a scene context feature is generated; s2, fusing the flight height as condition information into a flow matching network, enabling the network to output a plurality of pedestrian candidate prediction trajectories at a time, improving the spatial diversity of the plurality of candidate prediction trajectories through loss constraint, and outputting a multi-modal reference trajectory through multi-step integral sampling; s3, distilling the multi-step reasoning teacher model into a single-step reasoning student model through implicit maximum likelihood estimation by adopting a weighted loss function associated with the flight height; and S4, deploying the student model to the airborne edge computing device of the unmanned aerial vehicle.

sources.title: Robot target condition trajectory generation and planning method based on flow matching [CN122813864A]
sources.abstract: The invention relates to the technical field of robots, in particular to a robot target condition trajectory generating and planning method based on flow matching. The state of the robot at the current moment, the task target state and the accumulated return maximum value are obtained, and a condition vector is constructed; and sampling a plurality of noise tracks from the standard Gaussian distribution, and replacing the state of each noise track at the initial moment with the state of the robot at the current moment. And determining each candidate trajectory through the trained conditional velocity field network. And for each candidate trajectory, determining a first-step action of the candidate trajectory, and obtaining a value score of the first-step action based on the trained target condition value network. According to the sequence of the value scores of the first-step actions, target actions sent to the robot to be executed are determined, the target actions are sent to the robot, and after the state of the robot is updated, the steps are executed circularly. According to the scheme, the trajectory reasoning speed can be increased, and the real-time planning requirement of the robot is met.

sources.title: Molecular generation method based on pharmacophore perception prior and multi-target flow matching [CN122822142A]
authors: HUNAN UNIV OF TECHNOLOGY AND BUSINESS
sources.organization: HUNAN UNIV OF TECHNOLOGY AND BUSINESS
sources.abstract: The invention discloses a molecule generation method based on pharmacophore perception prior and multi-target flow matching, and relates to the technical field of artificial intelligence and computer-aided drug design. The method comprises the steps that the number of ligand atoms is determined, and the noise state is initialized; constructing a fusion guide velocity field, embedding multiple attribute constraints such as pharmacophore specificity, drug-likelihood, synthesis accessibility and the like into an unconditional vector field in a weighted projection mode, and resolving guide direction contradictions through a conflict perception mechanism; driving an ordinary differential equation solver from noise integration to a final state by using the velocity field, and performing discrete decoding on the final state to construct a molecular graph; effective molecules are screened through chemical valence and connectivity verification, and if the effective molecules do not pass the verification, resampling is triggered until the standard is reached or a retry upper limit is reached. Multi-target collaborative optimization is achieved, the generated molecules have high target combining capacity, good drug-likeness and synthesis feasibility, the structural effectiveness and space rationality are remarkably superior to those of an existing method, and the method is suitable for target-oriented rational drug design.

sources.title: Speech synthesis method and device, computer equipment and storage medium [CN122821925A]
authors: PING AN TECH SHENZHEN CO LTD
sources.organization: PING AN TECH SHENZHEN CO LTD
sources.abstract: The invention provides a speech synthesis method and device, computer equipment and a storage medium, and relates to the technical field of artificial intelligence. The method comprises the following steps: denoising sample Gaussian noise, reference voice, each denoising time and sample speaker characteristics through an initial flow matching model to obtain a prediction vector field; performing conditional loss calculation according to the prediction vector field, the sample Gaussian noise and the reference voice to obtain conditional flow matching loss data; carrying out loss calculation based on the sample speaker features and intermediate features output by the plurality of converters to obtain hierarchical speaker loss data; performing parameter adjustment on the initial stream matching model according to the two pieces of loss data to obtain a target stream matching model; and performing voice generation on the target text and the target speaker feature through the target stream matching model to obtain a target voice. The method is suitable for the financial field and the medical field, and can solve the technical problem that the consistency of the tone of the synthesized voice and the prompt tone is poor.

sources.title: Intelligent task flow dynamic arrangement and automatic ticket forming method, system and device for power distribution network dispatching service and medium [CN122819873A]
sources.abstract: The invention relates to the technical field of power distribution network dispatching automation and intelligent operation and maintenance management, and discloses an intelligent task flow dynamic arrangement and automatic ticket forming method, system and device for power distribution network dispatching businesses and a medium. Generating a structured normalized instruction; on the basis of the standardized instruction, automatically disassembling a complex scheduling instruction into executable action units; mapping each action unit into a predefined standard task type, and dynamically sorting the obtained standard tasks according to dependency constraints among the tasks to generate a standardized task flow; and based on the standardized task flow, matching a preset bill template, and automatically generating an operation bill. According to the method, the stability and reproducibility of conversion from the complex scheduling instruction to the operation task flow are remarkably improved, and the risk controllability and auditing capability of the system under the uncertain condition are enhanced.

sources.title: Transformer cooling and spraying system based on distributed intelligent buckles and control method [CN122815983A]
authors: SHIYAN POWER SUPPLY CO STATE GRID HUBEI ELECTRIC POWER CO LTD
SHIYAN JUNENG ELECTRIC POWER DESIGN CO LTD
sources.organization: SHIYAN POWER SUPPLY CO STATE GRID HUBEI ELECTRIC POWER CO LTD, SHIYAN JUNENG ELECTRIC POWER DESIGN CO LTD
sources.abstract: The invention discloses a transformer cooling and spraying system based on a distributed intelligent buckle and a control method, and relates to the technical field of intelligent cooling control of a power transformer. The transformer cooling and spraying system comprises a water tank dosing assembly, a partition spraying pipeline, a layered temperature measurement intelligent buckle, a radio frequency and infrared temperature measurement component and a spraying controller; the buckles collect heat dissipation and environment temperature in an isolated mode, the spray controller integrates the functions of global temperature division multi-priority working conditions, partition adjustment of spray flow, matching of pure water circulation, multi-layer sensing verification and remote operation and maintenance, the control method collects multi-source temperature, extracts temperature rise characteristics and disposes various equipment working conditions in a layered mode, and timing sequence AI recognition auxiliary regulation and control are supported. Temperature measurement environment interference is reduced, accurate fixed-point cooling is achieved, insulation hidden dangers are avoided, corrosion inhibition, water saving and automatic fault pushing capabilities are achieved, operation is stable, and operation and maintenance are convenient.

sources.title: Seamless sketch guide image restoration method based on streaming background trajectory alignment [CN122820497A]
sources.abstract: The invention discloses a seamless sketch guide image restoration method based on streaming background trajectory alignment. According to the method, a pre-trained flow matching generation model is used as a unified sampling model, and a de-noising sampling path of a generation area and a deterministic evolution track of an original background are subjected to forced alignment by adopting a flow type background track alignment reasoning strategy; the problems of boundary discontinuity and splicing traces caused by background area sampling drift in the local repairing process of an existing generation model are effectively solved, and higher-fidelity and seamless image synthesis is achieved. According to the method, a plug-and-play track correction mechanism without training is introduced, the limitation that an existing repair frame is poor in background consistency and stiff in transition when facing complex semantic structures and diversified sketch guidance is overcome, and experiments prove that the method has the advantages that the method has good application prospects in the aspects of reducing the perceptual difference (LPIPS), improving the structural fidelity (Edge-F1) and optimizing the boundary smoothness (G (at) e); the method is obviously superior to the prior art.

sources.title: Mobile device deployable video generation model and training method thereof [CN122824953A]
sources.abstract: The invention relates to the technical field of computer vision and machine learning, and discloses a mobile device deployable video generation model and a training method thereof.The method comprises the steps that firstly, based on the Taylor expansion principle, a parameter importance score is calculated, a teacher model redundant channel and an attention head are removed, and a compact student model is constructed and inherits a reserved weight; then, a double-flow parallel channel is constructed, and based on middle layer feature alignment, output distillation and flow matching diffusion loss joint optimization, the basic capacity is restored; then, utilizing the screened high-quality video training subsets to finely adjust the model only based on the stream matching loss under the condition of cutting off the teacher model constraint; and finally, calculating the distribution matching distillation gradient by using the difference between the real distribution score and the forged distribution score, and updating the model to enable the model to have a few-step reasoning capability. According to the invention, through a structure pruning and staged distillation strategy, the parameter quantity and the calculation complexity are reduced, and meanwhile, high-fidelity and low-delay video generation on the mobile terminal equipment is realized.

sources.title: Focus image generation type data enhancement method based on detector-guided adversarial flow matching [CN122798674A]
sources.abstract: The invention discloses a focus image generative data enhancement method based on detector-guided adversarial flow matching, and the method comprises the steps: constructing two decoupled flow matching generation models, the foreground generator is used for learning and generating a focus area image, and the background generator is used for learning and generating a focus-free background area image by adopting a feature isolation mechanism; applying adversarial disturbance in the sampling process of a foreground generator and a background generator by utilizing a focus detector through adversarial flow attack guided by the detector, and generating a false positive sample and a false negative sample; in the process of generating the false negative sample, a heuristic anchoring mechanism is introduced, a true positive sample and a true negative sample which are generated in advance are used as anchor points, and semantics of the false negative sample in a feature space is constrained; and adding the generated false positive samples and false negative samples into an original training set, and retraining the detector. According to the invention, a high-quality focus detection sample can be generated, and the robustness and generalization ability of a focus detection model are improved.

sources.title: Pressure and flow cooperative control method and system for precise energy-saving injection molding machine [CN122788224A]
authors: HONGZHENG LIANSU ZHEJIANG MACHINERY CO LTD
sources.organization: HONGZHENG LIANSU ZHEJIANG MACHINERY CO LTD
sources.abstract: The invention relates to the technical field of injection molding machines, in particular to a precise energy-saving injection molding machine pressure and flow cooperative control method and system. According to the method, the pressure evolution track is dynamically predicted, so that the defining of the rheological adaptive dynamic transition interval is based on the actual working condition, the pressure and flow closed-loop control loop can be synchronously adjusted when the injection molding machine is switched into the pressure maintaining stage, accurate real-time control is realized, and the real-time performance of the injection molding machine is improved by utilizing the apparent viscosity and the flow matching coefficient which are identified on line. The cooperative control output value is further optimized, the product defect risk caused by pressure fluctuation in the demolding process is reduced, self-adaptive correction of rheological parameters and transition intervals is achieved through a feedback mechanism and generation of process operation state quantity, it is ensured that the production requirements of high-precision products are efficiently met, and the product quality is improved. And the product quality and the production efficiency are improved.

sources.title: AI auxiliary inversion design method for broadband millimeter wave low-noise amplifier [CN122797448A]
sources.abstract: The invention belongs to the technical field of radio frequency integrated circuit automation design. The invention discloses a broadband millimeter wave low noise amplifier AI auxiliary inversion design method, which comprises the following steps: constructing a matching network model library, and carrying out waveform consistency verification on a front stage and a rear stage after splitting; carrying out full-wave simulation on the passive structure to obtain an impedance matrix and solving characteristic values, reconstructing a full-band S parameter by using four characteristic frequency points, and establishing a lightweight neural network agent model; an optimal algorithm is selected through adaptive scoring of the algorithm library, local sensitivity screening and front-and-back-stage alternating optimization are executed, and a candidate set is expanded in combination with flow matching; synchronously applying design rule constraints when the layout is generated; simulation is completed through Python-ADS automatic closed loop, and after data integrity check, an effective result is fed back to the model to achieve error-driven updating. The full-frequency simulation cost is remarkably reduced, the S11 mean value is improved by 1.05 dB, the gain flatness is improved by 0.41 dB, and the design period is shortened from about 2 weeks to about 1 day.

sources.title: True three-dimensional multi-modal space omics reconstruction method and system based on stream matching [CN122781382A]
authors: UNIV OF SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY OF CHINA
sources.organization: UNIV OF SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY OF CHINA
sources.abstract: The invention discloses a true three-dimensional multi-modal spatial omics reconstruction method and system based on flow matching, and the method comprises the steps: firstly obtaining the data of adjacent slices of a cell to be processed, extracting the spatial coordinates, high-dimensional omics characteristics and cell type data of the cell, and projecting the extracted data into a standardized space; calculating an unbalanced optimal transmission UOT soft coupling matrix between the cell slices based on the multi-modal cost matrix, and obtaining a target probability path of continuous evolution of the cells; a multi-modal flow matching model GiT is trained, and a continuous dynamic vector field representing the cell state evolution process is learned; under the guidance of an interpolation cell density field, inverse transformation sampling and a bidirectional ordinary differential equation ODE solving strategy are applied, integration is carried out along a continuous dynamic vector field, and a true three-dimensional cell state map of any physical depth is generated. And cross-modal compatibility and high-fidelity 3D reconstruction of heterogeneous data are realized.

sources.title: CT-free PET attenuation and scattering correction method based on visual language model prompt guidance [CN122780085A]
authors: SHENZHEN INST OF ADVANCED TECHNOLOGY CHINESE ACADEMY OF SCIENCES
sources.organization: SHENZHEN INST OF ADVANCED TECHNOLOGY CHINESE ACADEMY OF SCIENCES
sources.abstract: The invention discloses a CT-free PET attenuation and scattering correction method based on visual language model prompt guidance. The method comprises the following steps: obtaining an uncorrected PET image, and obtaining a corresponding organ-level text prompt by using a vision-language model; on the basis of the uncorrected PET image and the organ-level text prompt, a trained conditional flow matching model is used for obtaining a prediction feature field, then a corrected PET image is obtained, the conditional flow matching model is constructed in a submerged space and used for describing a continuous distribution mapping relation from the uncorrected PET image to the corrected PET image, and therefore the corrected PET image is obtained. And fusion of semantics and image features is realized through a cross attention mechanism. According to the method, the organ-level semantic prompt is generated by introducing the vision-language model, and is fused into the correction process, so that the effective utilization of the prior information of the anatomical structure is realized, and the structural consistency and the quantitative analysis accuracy of a complex region are improved.

sources.title: Public network IP automatic acceleration control method, device, equipment and medium [CN122783407A]
authors: PING AN TECH SHENZHEN CO LTD
sources.organization: PING AN TECH SHENZHEN CO LTD
sources.abstract: The invention relates to the field of network communication, and discloses a public network IP automatic acceleration control method and device, equipment and a medium, and the method comprises the steps: collecting the traffic data of a public network IP, and filtering the traffic data to obtain effective traffic data; obtaining an associated resource pool of an IP address corresponding to the effective flow data and an automatic acceleration strategy; performing caching and counting statistics on the effective flow data, and when a counting value meets a preset condition, calculating a bandwidth utilization rate corresponding to the associated resource pool and writing the bandwidth utilization rate into a cache; and performing bidirectional trend verification on the bandwidth utilization rate according to a flow matching rule in the automatic speed-up strategy, and if a speed-up triggering condition is met, obtaining a distributed lock and initiating a speed-up request so as to execute step-by-step speed-up operation until a target bandwidth is reached. The method can be applied to business scenes such as financial science and technology, medical health and the like, the speed-up strategy is self-defined through the resource pool, bidirectional verification and a distributed locking mechanism are combined, automatic speed-up strategy issuing and speed-up verification triggering are achieved, and the response speed of automatic speed-up and the system stability are improved.

sources.title: Building flow field prediction method and system based on conditional graph flow matching model [CN122758831A]
sources.abstract: The invention discloses a building flow field prediction method and system based on a conditional graph flow matching model, relates to prediction of a building flow field, and aims to solve the problem of low prediction accuracy of the building flow field. Comprising the following steps: acquiring flow field sample data of each streaming object to obtain a flow field data set; representing simulated flow field sample data as a graph structure; constructing a hierarchical graph neural network and configuring a loss function, and training a conditional velocity field to enable the conditional velocity field to fit a target velocity field; obtaining to-be-predicted flow field data; an initial noise field with the same dimension as a physical field on a graph node is sampled from standard Gaussian distribution, and the current flow field is iteratively updated by using a condition velocity field obtained by training; and after multi-step iteration, a final flow field generation result is obtained. Based on a condition graph flow matching model, a probability path from Gaussian prior to target distribution is constructed on flow time, flow field data meeting given geometric and boundary conditions and physical parameter constraints can be generated, and the building flow field prediction accuracy is improved.

sources.title: Robot operation method and system based on multi-Gaussian mixed flow matching strategy [CN122759402A]
authors: QILU UNIV OF TECHNOLOGY SHANDONG ACADEMY OF SCIENCES
sources.organization: UNIV TIANJIN TECHNOLOGY, SHANDONG ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE RESEARCH INST, QILU UNIV OF TECHNOLOGY SHANDONG ACADEMY OF SCIENCES
sources.abstract: The invention discloses a robot operation method and system based on a multi-Gaussian mixed flow matching strategy, and relates to the technical field of imitation learning. The method specifically comprises the following steps: re-parameterizing a stream matching target into a dynamic Gaussian mixture model, predicting a mixed weight, a component mean value and a shared covariance through a residual MLP backbone network and a parallel parameter header, and explicitly retaining a plurality of action modes; in the training stage, combined optimization of Gaussian mixture negative logarithm likelihood loss and adaptive speed matching loss is adopted; in the inference stage, an entropy-guided adaptive sampling mechanism is introduced, mixed mean prediction and maximum probability mode prediction are adaptively fused according to Shannon entropy of Gaussian mixture distribution, and few-step action generation is performed through Euler integral. According to the method, high-quality actions can be generated under the condition of few-step or even single-step reasoning, meanwhile, execution failures caused by multi-mode action averaging are effectively avoided, and the method is suitable for robot grabbing, stacking, assembling and other long-time-sequence operation tasks.

draft.summary: Research activity on flow matching is rising very fast: OpenAlex works with the phrase went from 203 in 2024 to 837 in 2025, and 3,399 by 28 Oct 2026 against 637 at the same point in 2025. The science findings show a mature core method (S1, S11) that is being extended to discrete data, scientific inference, robotics and symmetry-aware graphs (S2, S6, S7, S8). Patent filings also rise (143 in 2025; 307 by 28 Oct 2026 against 103 a year earlier). They are mostly from Chinese academic institutions, and keyword noise affects the search (P4, P5). The Risk agent documents recurring training instability and narrow, often unreplicated few-step benchmarks (R1-R7), and challenges the strength of several science claims (C1-C6). The Market agent found no relevant company evidence: every hit was pension 'cash flow matching' language, so there is no evidence on products, customers, investment or supply chain (M1, M4). The main uncertainty is whether the research boom converts into products that paying customers use. These findings do not answer that.
draft.plain_summary: Flow matching is a way of training AI systems to generate things like images, video, molecules and robot movements. The number of research papers and patent applications about it is growing very quickly. We found no evidence yet of companies selling products built on it. Reported training instability and thinly tested speed claims could slow the move from lab results to real use.

No company or customer evidence was found (M4), so near-term commercial conversion is not supported.
